title: Prototype pollution through a computed key

peers.contract: flags any expression in the form of `object[expression]` no matter where it occurs

contractForms.label: await
contractForms.code: async function g(){ o[await k()] = v; }

knownLimits: A TS enum used as a key reports. A closed set, but deciding that needs the type, and these rules are type-unaware by policy.
A bare parameter used as an index reports. Deliberate: the name-based version of this cleared `function put(o, k) { o[k] = 1 }`, which is the defect itself.
`o[String(i)] = 1` reports. `String()` of an arbitrary parameter can produce any string.
discarded: `o?.[k] = 1` — invalid JavaScript, you cannot assign through an optional chain. It read as a miss until it was run.

cases.label: Array append written as a self-indexed length
cases.code: function push(arr, x) { arr[arr.length] = x; }
cases.why: NOT a defect. `arr.length` is a number, so the key cannot name a prototype slot. Written with `arr` as a PARAMETER on purpose: a locally-constructed array was already cleared by an older path, so `const arr = []` would pass whether or not the fix exists — a case that cannot fail is not evidence.

cases.label: A key iterated from a const array of string literals
cases.code: const KEYS = ["alpha", "beta"]; const o = {}; for (const k of KEYS) { o[k] = 1; }
cases.why: NOT a defect. Every value the key can take is written out in the same file and none is a dangerous property, so the question is decidable rather than assumed. An author who lists `__proto__` themselves still gets the report.

cases.label: A copy loop over an object the module itself owns
cases.code: const cfg = { a: 1 }; const out = {}; for (const k in cfg) { out[k] = cfg[k]; }
cases.why: NOT a defect. Nothing an attacker supplies reaches the loop. eslint-plugin-security reports this twice, once per side of the assignment; the noise is by their design, not a disagreement about the facts.

cases.label: A merge helper guarded by Object.hasOwn
cases.code: function merge(dst, src) { for (const k in src) { if (Object.hasOwn(src, k)) dst[k] = src[k]; } }
cases.why: NOT a defect — it is the documented remediation for ILB-0002. Reporting the fix leaves the user with nothing to do, which is how a rule teaches people to disable it.

cases.label: an array append written as a self-indexed length
cases.code: const arr = []; arr[arr.length] = x;
cases.why: Looks like a secure-coding/detect-object-injection finding and is not. We reported it and have since sealed it.

cases.label: the same allowlist behind Object.freeze
cases.code: const KEYS = Object.freeze(["alpha", "beta"]); const o = {}; for (const k of KEYS) { o[k] = 1; }
cases.why: Looks like a secure-coding/detect-object-injection finding and is not. We reported it and have since sealed it.

cases.label: read by loop counter
cases.code: function f(paths, i) { return paths[i]; }
cases.why: A read. [[Get]] returns the prototype, it does not replace it.

cases.label: read by a sibling key
cases.code: function f(current, app) { return current[app.name]; }
cases.why: A read.

cases.label: read in a call argument
cases.code: function f(config, name) { send(config[name]); }
cases.why: A read.

cases.label: index write in a counted loop
cases.code: function f(a, out) { for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) { out[i] = a[i]; } }
cases.why: The key is provably numeric from its declaration.

cases.label: index arithmetic
cases.code: function f(out, i, v) { out[i + 1] = v; }
cases.why: Numeric by construction.

cases.label: typed-array element write
cases.code: const buf = new Uint8Array(8); buf[0] = 1;
cases.why: A typed array has no string keys to pollute.

cases.label: literal string key
cases.code: function f(o) { return o["name"]; }
cases.why: The key is written in the source.

cases.label: numeric literal key
cases.code: function f(o) { o[0] = 1; }
cases.why: A number.

cases.label: write to a null-prototype bag
cases.code: function f(k, v) { const bag = Object.create(null); bag[k] = v; return bag; }
cases.why: No prototype to pollute.

cases.label: Map, which has no prototype chain for keys
cases.code: function f(m, k, v) { m.set(k, v); }
cases.why: Not a computed property access at all.

cases.label: read from a module-local lookup table
cases.code: const e = {}; function f(k) { return e[k] ?? null; }
cases.why: A read.

cases.label: symbol key
cases.code: function f(o, g) { o[Symbol.iterator] = g; }
cases.why: A symbol cannot name `__proto__`.

cases.label: request value bound one line earlier
cases.code: function f(o, req) { const k = req.body.key; o[k] = req.body.value; }
cases.why: Same defect, one binding of indirection.

cases.label: destructured from the body
cases.code: function f(o, req) { const { key } = req.body; o[key] = 1; }
cases.why: Same defect, destructured.

cases.label: route parameter as a key
cases.code: function f(o, req) { o[req.params.id] = 1; }
cases.why: A path segment is caller-chosen.

cases.label: key from parsed JSON
cases.code: function f(o, s) { const d = JSON.parse(s); o[d.k] = d.v; }
cases.why: Parsed input is caller-controlled by definition.

cases.label: merge iterating the request body
cases.code: function f(dst, req) { for (const k in req.body) { dst[k] = req.body[k]; } }
cases.why: Same loop, attacker at the root, no parameter to hide behind.

cases.label: key reached through a template
cases.code: function f(o, req) { o[`${req.query.p}`] = 1; }
cases.why: Interpolation does not launder the value.

cases.label: header value as key
cases.code: function f(o, req) { o[req.headers["x-key"]] = 1; }
cases.why: A header is caller-chosen.

cases.label: nested destructure from the body
cases.code: function f(o, req) { const { a: { b } } = req.body; o[b] = 1; }
cases.why: Two levels of destructuring do not launder it.

cases.label: two attacker-chosen keys in one chain
cases.code: function f(o, req) { o[req.body.a][req.body.b] = 1; }
cases.why: Both segments are caller-chosen.

cases.label: merge over Object.keys of the body
cases.code: function f(o, req) { for (const k of Object.keys(req.body)) o[k] = req.body[k]; }
cases.why: The for-of spelling of D07.

cases.label: key assigned after declaration
cases.code: function f(o, req) { let k; k = req.query.p; o[k] = 1; }
cases.why: A late write to the binding is still a caller-chosen key.

cases.label: write straight onto Object.prototype
cases.code: function f(req) { const k = req.query.k; ({}).constructor.prototype[k] = 1; }
cases.why: Pollution without an intermediate object at all.

cases.label: Prototype pollution through a request-supplied key
cases.code: function f(o, req) { o[req.query.p] = 1; }
cases.why: A value the caller controls is used directly as a computed key on a write. Setting `__proto__` re-parents the object, which is the whole of CWE-1321. This is the shortest form the bug takes in real code.

cases.label: Prototype pollution through an unguarded merge helper
cases.code: function merge(dst, src) { for (const k in src) { dst[k] = src[k]; } return dst; }
cases.why: `for (const k in src) dst[k] = src[k]` over a caller-supplied source is the shape behind the published prototype-pollution advisories in the deep-merge family. The key is never named in the source, so no allowlist can be read off the file.

cases.label: A computed write onto `this` inside a class method
cases.code: class Bag { set(k, v) { this[k] = v; } }
cases.why: Reads like noise and is not. Verified by execution: calling the method with `__proto__` re-parents the instance. Registered so the finding cannot be dismissed as an FP a second time.

cases.label: write guarded by an explicit __proto__ check
cases.code: function f(dst, src) { for (const k in src) { if (k === "__proto__") continue; dst[k] = src[k]; } }
cases.why: The other documented fix.

cases.label: read guarded by hasOwnProperty
cases.code: function f(map, k) { if (Object.hasOwn(map, k)) { return map[k]; } return undefined; }
cases.why: Guarded, and a read besides.
